title: Whispering DNS
subtitle: Decode data exfiltration hidden in DNS queries
summary: An egress sensor captured a short DNS session. Most lookups are ordinary, but three queries carry hex-encoded payloads. Extract them, decode the token and document the exfiltration.
scenario: Vela Retail's egress filter allows DNS out of the datacenter. A sensor capture from the same window shows a workstation talking to an unfamiliar subdomain. Reconstruct what left the network and produce an evidence record.
prerequisites: Familiarity with grep or a pcap tool
learningObjectives: Inspect real pcap bytes without a GUI
Reassemble split encoded payloads in order
authorizedScope: Only the synthetic capture in this workspace. Addresses and domains are fictional.
riskSummary: DNS tunnelling survives many egress controls because DNS is almost always permitted. Data can leave in label chunks that look like noise to naive filters.
remediation: Send DNS through a logging resolver, alert on long or high-entropy labels, enforce allow-listed resolvers, and block recursive lookups for uncategorised domains.
conclusion: You separated benign lookups from three encoded queries, reassembled and hex-decoded them into the exfiltration token, and documented the tunnel.

objectives.title: Decode the DNS exfiltration
objectives.description: Pull the hex labels that were queried under exfil.vela-retail.example, concatenate them in capture order and hex-decode the result to recover the token.

hints.text: `strings ~/artifacts/capture.pcap | grep exfil` shows the query names; the sublabels are hex, not words.
Both hex chunks arrive in one query as two sub-labels. Join them and decode: `python3 -c "import sys;print(bytes.fromhex('hexhere'))"`.

objectives.title: Document the tunnel
objectives.description: Complete evidence/dns-exfil.json with the exfil domain, the encoded labels and the decoded token, plus notes on how the data left.

hints.text: Order matters: use the labels as they appear in the capture.

walkthrough.title: Find the queries
walkthrough.body: Read the capture as bytes and look for the exfiltration domain.

walkthrough.title: Decode the labels
walkthrough.body: Concatenate the two hex sub-labels of the suspicious query, then hex-decode them.
walkthrough.snippet: python3 ~/tools/dnsq.py ~/artifacts/capture.pcap | grep exfil | cut -d. -f1,2 | tr -d "." | python3 -c "import sys;print(bytes.fromhex(sys.stdin.read().strip()).decode())"

walkthrough.title: Write the evidence
walkthrough.body: Store the domain, labels and token, then run the objective check.
walkthrough.snippet: jq -n '{exfilDomain:"exfil.vela-retail.example",encodedLabels:["..."],decodedFlag:"CF{...}",notes:"Hex chunks split across DNS labels under an allow-listed resolver"}' > ~/evidence/dns-exfil.json
